_real_world.class: Type 366 / Mineral-ME-derived surface-search and over-the-horizon targeting radar
_real_world.variant_scope: Type 054A (and reported on Type 055 as a secondary set); reused where a hull's surface-search fit is not separately characterized.
public_equipment: Type 366 / Mineral-ME surface-search and OTH targeting radar

_provenance.modeling_note: Surface-search / over-the-horizon anti-ship targeting radar for Type 054A per GlobalSecurity (C-only); a blog-sourced Fregat-MAE-5 range figure ('120 km aircraft / 50 km sea-skimmer') is C-only and not from a Type-366-specific source, so it is used only as loose reasoning, not carried directly. Modeled as a shorter-range dedicated surface-search set distinct from the packet's air-search AESA/3D radar modules.

sensor.type.note: Type 366 is a surface-search/OTH targeting radar; Radar is the matching engine sensor type

sensor.max_range.note: no dedicated Type 366 range figure; a blog-sourced 'Fregat-MAE-5, 50 km vs sea-skimmer' figure exists but is not confirmed as the same system, so this is an engineering estimate for a dedicated surface-search radar's sea-skimmer detection range, roughly consistent with that reasoning

sensor.fov_deg.note: 360 deg: standard convention for a rotating surface-search radar

sensor.scan_period.note: no public rotation-rate figure; engineering estimate typical of a rotating surface-search radar

sensor.detection_prob.note: no public Pd figure; engineering estimate for a dedicated surface-search radar against surface/low-altitude targets

sensor.bearing_noise_std.note: no public bearing-accuracy figure; engineering estimate for a surface-search radar

sensor.range_noise_std.note: no public range-accuracy figure; engineering estimate for a surface-search radar

sensor.track_memory_s.note: no public track-coast figure; engineering estimate typical of a surface-search radar

sensor.range_power.note: radar-equation exponent (inverse-4th-power family); standard engine default, not sourced per-platform

sensor.aspect_influence.note: 0.0 disables RCS aspect-angle modeling, consistent with this packet's simplified surface-search detection model

sensor.doppler_notch_width.note: no public MTI/doppler-notch figure; engineering estimate for a surface-search radar

sensor.reference_snr_db.note: radar-equation calibration constant paired with reference_range_m/reference_rcs_m2 to reproduce max_range at a reference target; no public figure

sensor.reference_range_m.note: paired radar-equation calibration constant, see reference_snr_db

sensor.reference_rcs_m2.note: 5 m^2 generic warship reference RCS, engine convention used across this packet's naval radar records

sensor.antenna_height_m.note: no public mast height; engineering estimate for a lower secondary-mast surface-search antenna, below the packet's air-search modules

sensor.target_height_bias_m.note: no public figure; engineering estimate lower than the packet's air-search modules, consistent with a surface-search radar's sea-skimmer-oriented geometry

sensor.environment_domain.note: surface/maritime domain selected for a shipborne surface-search radar per authoring standard

sensor.sea_clutter_enabled.note: disabled, consistent with this packet's simplified detection model; no sourced clutter-suppression figure exists to calibrate an enabled model

sensor.enable_ducting.note: standard engine atmospheric-ducting toggle, enabled with a small gain/bonus consistent with a shorter-range surface-search radar

sensor.ducting_gain_factor.note: engineering estimate, lower than the packet's long-range air-search AESA modules

sensor.ducting_max_bonus_m.note: engineering estimate, lower than the packet's long-range air-search AESA modules

modeling_notes: Reused as the sensor_refs surface-search entry for hulls whose escort-specific surface-search set is not separately characterized in the OOB (052D's Type 364, 055's secondary surface-search fit), per authoring standard's rule allowing reuse of an existing module when no hull-specific one is written, noted here rather than writing near-duplicate records with no distinguishing sourced data.
